theory.intro: Angle pairs are named either by where the angles sit or by what their measures add to.
facts: **Complementary** angles have measures that add to $90^{\circ}$.
**Supplementary** angles have measures that add to $180^{\circ}$.
One pair can fit more than one name; adjacent angles can also be complementary.

workedExamples.question_text: Decide whether angles measuring $38^{\circ}$ and $52^{\circ}$ are complementary, supplementary, or neither.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Complementary angles sum to $90^{\circ}$.
$90 - 36 = 54$.
The complement is $54^{\circ}$.

Supplementary angles sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$180 - 124 = 56$.
The supplement is $56^{\circ}$.

They share vertex $V$ and arm $VQ$.
They do not overlap.
The angles are adjacent.

foundation.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.75]\draw (-2,-1.4)--(2,1.4);\draw (-2,1.4)--(2,-1.4);\draw (0.45,0.32) arc[start angle=35,end angle=145,radius=0.55];\draw (-0.45,-0.32) arc[start angle=215,end angle=325,radius=0.55];\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Identify the relationship between the two marked angles.
foundation.solution_text:
The marked angles are opposite each other where two straight lines intersect.
They are vertically opposite angles.

foundation.question_text: Which relationship describes angles measuring $32^{\circ}$ and $58^{\circ}$?
Which relationship describes angles measuring $117^{\circ}$ and $63^{\circ}$?

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.7]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\draw (O)--(2,0) node[right] {$A$};\draw (O)--(1.2,1.7) node[above] {$B$};\draw (O)--(-1.5,1.3) node[above] {$C$};\node[below] at (O) {$O$};\draw (0.5,0) arc[start angle=0,end angle=55,radius=0.5];\draw (0.42,0.6) arc[start angle=55,end angle=139,radius=0.72];\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Identify the relationship between $\angle AOB$ and $\angle BOC$.
foundation.solution_text:
They share vertex $O$ and arm $OB$, and do not overlap.
They are adjacent angles.

development.solution_text:
$OC$ is opposite $OA$, and $OD$ is opposite $OB$.
The vertically opposite angle is $\angle COD$.

development.question_text: From $24^{\circ}$, $66^{\circ}$ and $156^{\circ}$, choose the angle complementary to $24^{\circ}$.
From $42^{\circ}$, $138^{\circ}$ and $148^{\circ}$, choose the angle supplementary to $42^{\circ}$.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.7]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\foreach \a/\n in {10/A,70/B,155/C,240/D}{\draw (O)--(\a:2) node[anchor=180+\a] {$\n$};}\node[below] at (O) {$O$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Are $\angle AOB$ and $\angle COD$ adjacent?
Give the positional reason.
development.solution_text: No. They share a vertex but do not share an arm.

mastery.solution_text:
Both angles share vertex $O$ and arm $OC$.
However, $\angle BOC$ lies inside $\angle AOC$, so they overlap.
They are not adjacent.

mastery.question_text: Decide whether angles measuring $73.5^{\circ}$ and $106.25^{\circ}$ are complementary, supplementary, or neither.
mastery.solution_text:
$73.5 + 106.25 = 179.75$.
The total is neither $90^{\circ}$ nor $180^{\circ}$.
The angles are neither complementary nor supplementary.
